title: NATO leaders issue Vilnius Summit Communique and create the NATO-Ukraine Council
body:
NATO heads of state and government issued the Vilnius Summit Communique on 11 July 2023 during a summit in the Lithuanian capital. On Ukraine, allies reaffirmed the commitment made at the 2008 Bucharest summit that Ukraine will become a member of the alliance. They stated that Ukraine's path to Euro-Atlantic integration no longer required the Membership Action Plan.

The communique said allies would keep supporting and reviewing Ukraine's reforms, with NATO foreign ministers assessing progress regularly. It contained the wording: "We will be in a position to extend an invitation to Ukraine to join the Alliance when Allies agree and conditions are met." It did not set a timetable for an invitation.

Allies also created the NATO-Ukraine Council, a body in which allies and Ukraine sit as equal members. It was intended to advance political dialogue and cooperation, support Ukraine's aspirations for membership, and serve as a mechanism for consultation in a crisis.

The communique also addressed Sweden's accession. Allies welcomed an agreement reached between NATO Secretary General Jens Stoltenberg, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson, and stated that they looked forward to welcoming Sweden as a full member of the alliance. The summit took place during the first weeks of Ukraine's summer counteroffensive against Russian forces.
